## Circular to Licensed Corporations Business continuity planning against serious communicable diseases

Drawing  lessons  from  the  recent  Severe  Acute  Respiratory  Syndrome  ('SARS')  outbreak and in light of the warning from health officials that it could become a seasonal hazard, the Commission would like to remind licensed persons to take precautions against a reoccurrence of SARS or other serious communicable diseases.

The  Commission  is  concerned  of  the  potential  disruption  to  intermediaries'  operations resulting from their staff members' infection.  As part of your business continuity plan, please ensure that the following measures are considered:

1. follow  the  Department  of  Health's  guidance  in  maintaining  a  clean  and  healthy working environment;
2. encourage staff to maintain  good personal hygiene;
3. review,  revise  or  devise  policies  and  procedures  to  ensure  business  continuity  or prevent material disruption to your operation in the event of staff infection.  These may include (but are not limited to):
- establishing  a  crisis  management  structure  for  information  sharing,  corporate decision  making  and  revising  arrangements  in  accordance  with  changing circumstances;
- arranging for a (reciprocal) back-up office;
- setting up of different critical operational teams;
- arranging for operational teams to work at compatible remote premises where feasible;
- arranging  with  counterparts  or  exchanges  on  contingency  closing  out  of positions, clearing and settlement matters;
- encouraging  clients  to  use  telephone  or  online  facilities  in  place  of  physical visits;
- ensuring  reliability  of  telephone  recording  system  and  sufficiency  of  back  up discs/tapes etc;

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

![Image](data:image/png;base64,)

- reviewing system capacity to cater for potential upsurge in transaction volume in the event of clients massively switching  to using electronic channels;
- ensuring adequate back up facilities, mobile computing/communication devices and network bandwidth;
- establishing  client  notification  procedures  upon  staff  infection  and  advising clients on the relevant contingency measures;
- checking that your critical suppliers and service providers are equally prepared;
- arranging for rehearsal and testing of contingency plans, systems and equipment; and
4. last but not the least, notify your Licensing relationship manager promptly should any of your staff member become infected of any serious communicable disease, and keep the Commission apprised of any subsequent developments.

Intermediaries and Investment Products Division Securities and Futures Commission
